result.reason: Press (La Gazette des Comores, 2022-23) confirms the Ministry classifies private schools A/B/C, publishes lists of authorised schools, and requires dossiers. I found no official text, fee, or deadline, so the legal basis, frequency, and penalty are unverified. Counts differ: about 270-300 per the claim, 302 category-B schools and about 400 in the coordination census per press. No Comoros-specific school software turned up in two searches. Only generic tools (Kolonell, Senegal; Appvizer products; e-Shiyo, a public learning platform) appeared. The duty looks informal and irregular, and the buyers are small and low-paying. The dossier is a one-off submission to the ministry, and a tool that submits it has little value without fees tracking or a bulletin product. Score stays at 3.

decisions.reason: Private schools are small community bodies with a mandatory annual authorisation and dossier duty to the Ministry; new buyer and duty.
Food importers and establishments owe INRAPE inspection and agrément compliance, a different buyer and duty from K03 (customs brokers).
No mandatory authority-imposed traceability duty found; the demand is buyer or certification driven, so it fails the mandatory-workflow rule.
Fuel station operators have licensing and allocation reporting to the SCH and the Energy ministry; small-firm duty in scope.
Small decentralised financial institutions have recurring BCC reporting duties; different buyer from K01 to K03.
Small mobile money agent shops owe KYC and registration duties under BCC and payment rules; in scope.
Real estate promoters hold approval and sales compliance duties under Loi 17-001/AU; unverified, so keep.
Pharmacies and medicine wholesalers owe ANAMEV import authorisation, a different buyer and duty from K03 (related K03).
Small vessel owners owe registry and authorisation duties to ANAM; unverified, so keep.
Taxi and moto-taxi owners face recurring licence, insurance and registration checks; unverified, so keep.
Artisanal fishers have licence and catch recording duties under the fisheries code; weak but unverified, so keep.
Hotels, guest houses and travel agencies need tourism-law agrément and classification; unverified, so keep.
Vets, vet-drug sellers and livestock keepers face new duties under the 2026 Code de l'Elevage; new buyer and duty.
Village water committees are community bodies with accounts and tariff reporting duties; new buyer group.
Jewellers and gold dealers are designated non-financial businesses with AML/CFT duties; unverified, so keep.
Quarry operators owe impact studies and permits to the authorities; small firms in scope, unverified, so keep.
